about: Deleting a photo doesn't delete it. Factory #26, backlog row 30, slug deletephoto. One hard idea: on iPhone, Delete only moves a photo into the Recently Deleted album, where it waits 30 days (locked with Face ID or Touch ID by default); Google Photos keeps deleted items in Trash for 30 days; a copy a friend saved from your shared album stays in their library; it is only gone when you empty Recently Deleted or Trash, and then Apple and Google say it can't be recovered. Primary sources (read 2026-11-09): Apple Support 'Delete photos on your iPhone or iPad' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/104967, published Mar 31, 2026); Apple Support 'How to recover deleted photos on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/124460, published Sep 15, 2025); Apple Support 'How to use Shared Albums in Photos' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/108314, published Oct 6, 2026); Google Photos Help 'Delete photos & videos' (https://support.google.com/photos/answer/6128858) and 'Restore recently deleted photos & videos' (https://support.google.com/photos/answer/9343482). Native move: a 30-day tear-off calendar on the Recently Deleted bin. Planned silences: 0.8 s after 'theirs' (dip stamp), 1.0 s after 'gone' (hero stamp CAN'T GET IT BACK). Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times.

lines.text: Your deleted photos are still here.
Open Photos. Swipe up to Recently Deleted.
lines.say: Open Photos. Swipe up, to Recently Deleted.

lines.text: So when is a photo really gone?
lines.say: So, when is a photo really gone?

lines.text: Hit delete, and your iPhone just moves it there.
It waits there thirty days, locked by default.
Google Photos keeps its trash thirty days too.
But a friend who saved it from your shared album?
lines.say: But, a friend who saved it from your shared album?

lines.text: Their copy stays, even if you delete the album.
To really delete it, empty Recently Deleted or Trash.
lines.say: To really delete it, empty Recently Deleted, or Trash.

lines.text: Then, Apple and Google say, you can't get it back.
So, is yours empty? Yes or no.
lines.say: So, is yours empty, yes or no?
